Employees who have access to important information and key decision-makers tend to trust their company more. The goal is to help people who are working remotely maintain communication with you, your team, and senior leaders.

##### Collect and share stories
Look for examples of leaders' actions that show their personal side and convey the right company values. Share positive stories about senior leaders with your team and vice versa. This will help each group understand the other and feel a sense of shared success.

##### Be nearby even if you are far away
To build strong connections with a team that you don't see every day, you must understand each team member's experiences and needs, and seek out the appropriate support for them.  

Ask your team members how they are doing, if they need any support, and what concerns they have about the business. 

Ask them to help you build a case for any resources they may need.  

Make a commitment to them to secure necessary resources from senior leaders and to pass along their concerns about the business. Be specific about when and how you will do that, and how you will keep them informed. Be clear and concise about when and why you chose not to pursue a particular request.
